title: External write and telemetry registry
description: The enumerated declaration `scripts/template/telemetry-contract.ts` validates. Credential presence alone must not authorize a remote write, so a write is declared here with its intent, its credentials, the command that reads the remote back afterwards, and the exact hosts it may reach — and a tree that performs a write shape this file does not name is a refusal. `mode` is the load-bearing field: `skeleton` asserts, positively, that no telemetry surface and no undeclared write shape exists anywhere in the tracked tree; `active` asserts every declared path exists and runs every rule over it.

mode.description: The declared tree state. It is compared with the derived state before any other rule runs, and a disagreement in either direction is the first error.

telemetry.description: The centralized telemetry configuration, or null when this project sends none. Centralized means allowlist-not-denylist: the SDK may be imported and initialized only inside a module named here, and a project extends the allowlist by declaring a module rather than by weakening the guard.

configModules.description: Every module allowed to import and initialize the telemetry SDK. One tier per module, because a browser tier and a server tier are two different bundles with two different leak surfaces.

scrubModule.description: The one pure, SDK-free module every tier routes its payloads through. It is SDK-free on purpose: that is what lets a browser tier and a server tier share one scrubber instead of maintaining two that drift.

sendDefaultPii.description: Pinned false. There is no configuration in which a template ships default PII collection, so the field exists to be asserted rather than to be chosen.

tunnel.description: The same-origin path browser payloads are relayed through, or null when payloads go straight to the ingest host. Declared-or-explicitly-null: a project that never considered the question is a different state from one that decided against it.

dsnVariable.description: The environment variable carrying the ingest DSN. The DSN is a PUBLIC value — it ships inside the client bundle — so this name is checked for the opposite property from the upload token's: it may not read like a secret.

upload.description: The build-time artifact upload, or null when this project uploads nothing. The gate is intent times credential and never an environment flag: a plain local build sets neither variable and therefore never writes, even when a deployment token has leaked into the shell.

releaseVariable.description: The INTENT half. A release name is a deliberate statement that this build is a deployable artifact.

tokenVariable.description: The CREDENTIAL half, which must be credential-named because it is one.

scope.description: Which bundle the upload may reach. `server` is declarable so that the guard's refusal of it is reachable and testable rather than hypothetical.

writes.description: Every remote mutation this project performs, with the intent that authorizes it, the credentials it needs, and the separate read-only command that asserts the final remote state afterwards.

command.description: The mutating command itself. Declared so that the read-only verifier can be asserted to be a DIFFERENT string: a verifier that shares the writer's code path can only confirm what the writer believed.

intent.description: The named confirmation the write refuses to run without. A credential plus a flag is still not enough; a mutation needs a confirmation somebody had to type.

credentials.description: Every environment variable the write reads. Absence is a clean no-op, never a failure.

verify.description: The read-only command that queries the resource back after the write. It is a distinct declared command and never a flag on the write, because a verifier that shares the writer's code path can only confirm what the writer believed.

allowedHosts.description: The exact origins this write may reach. A subset of the top-level allowlist, with no wildcard entry.

The union every declared write's hosts must be a subset of. Exact origins only: a wildcard entry is a suppressed safety guard, and an allowlist that can match a host nobody enumerated is a denylist wearing an allowlist's name.

governedElsewhere.description: Write-shaped files whose rules already have an owner. Without this list the write-shape scan would be a scan with nothing to find, because the one remote write this repository performs is governed by a module that predates this registry.

relativePath.description: A repository-relative POSIX path. Absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected so a declaration cannot name a file outside the tree the guard scans.
